headline: Tech Selloff Steals the Show as Geopolitical Jitters Keep Bulls at Bay
body_html:
Monday's session closed on a sour note, with declining issues outpacing advancers by a ratio of roughly 341 to 206 across our 549-name universe. The dominant narrative was unmistakable: investors retreated from technology — semiconductors shed nearly 2.8% as a group, the worst of any sector — while escalating tensions surrounding Iran and the prospect of fresh U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods darkened the mood from the opening bell.

The sole pockets of resilience were tucked inside the consumer complex. Homebuilders edged up 0.6% and broader consumer names added 0.55%, suggesting that rate-sensitive and discretionary buyers found selective footing even as the wider market slid. Software dipped a modest 0.24%, but industrials, materials, healthcare, and energy all posted meaningful losses, reinforcing the session's defensive tilt away from growth.

The standout mover on the upside was Celsius Holdings, which surged more than 5% to lead the gainers board — a conspicuous bright spot amid otherwise heavy consumer-adjacent activity. On the downside, Azenta cratered more than 12%, the sharpest single-name drop of the day, underscoring the pressure on life-science tools names. With geopolitical crosscurrents multiplying and earnings risk alive in the chip space, Monday offered a reminder that conviction remains thin beneath the surface.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Slump Leads Sector Damage as Chip Names Bear the Brunt
briefs.body: Semiconductors fell nearly 2.83% on Monday, the ugliest sector reading of the session. Investors weighed the prospect of additional U.S. tariffs targeting Chinese overcapacity — reportedly as high as 7.5% ahead of potential Xi-Trump talks — alongside pre-earnings anxiety in the chip space. Memory and foundry names were not spared, though United Microelectronics bucked the trend with a gain of roughly 3.9%.

briefs.headline: Iran Tensions Color Market Sentiment; Threat of Broader Escalation Lingers
briefs.body: Geopolitical uncertainty tied to Iran weighed on risk appetite throughout Monday's session. Reports that Israel's prime minister claimed Iran attempted to harm a family member, combined with ongoing U.S. threats targeting nations that conduct business with Tehran, kept investors cautious. Markets in Europe also reflected the unease, closing broadly flat as participants awaited further developments.

briefs.headline: Celsius Holdings Surges More Than 5%, Tops the Day's Leaderboard
briefs.body: The energy-drink maker was the session's most notable gainer, climbing 5.01% to claim the top spot among advancers. The move extended a pattern of consumer-beverage resilience even as broader market conditions deteriorated. Vital Farms and Dutch Bros also posted gains above 4%, reinforcing the relative strength visible across consumer-facing names on Monday.

briefs.headline: Azenta Plunges 12%, Hims & Hers Slides Nearly 8% in Healthcare Rout
briefs.body: Healthcare was among the weaker sectors Monday, falling roughly 0.91% in aggregate, but the pain was most acute at the single-stock level. Azenta — a life-science tools provider — shed more than 12%, the steepest decline in our universe for the session. Telehealth name Hims & Hers dropped nearly 8%, adding to a difficult day for health-oriented growth equities.

briefs.headline: Storage and Database Names Hit Hard as Tech Rotation Bites
briefs.body: MongoDB fell 6.53% and Seagate Technology lost 6.51%, while Sandisk dropped 6.45%, forming a cluster of severe losses in storage-adjacent technology. The declines pointed to broad-based selling pressure in data-infrastructure names rather than any single company-specific catalyst, consistent with the wider retreat from growth and technology assets across the session.

briefs.headline: France and Saudi Arabia Ink Agreement on Multibillion-Euro Theme-Park Venture
briefs.body: In a deal that caught markets' attention outside the usual financial sphere, France and Saudi Arabia reached an agreement on a roughly €6 billion Dragon Ball Z-themed entertainment complex to be built near Paris. The announcement signals continued Gulf sovereign appetite for high-profile Western leisure and tourism assets, a trend worth monitoring for related hospitality and construction sectors.
